key_insight: Pathology foundation models can retrieve morphologically similar salivary gland tumor cases from an archive without task-specific training, helping extend case-based diagnosis to rare subtypes.
clinical_relevance: This could make departmental whole-slide archives searchable for differential diagnosis support, especially when rare tumors fall outside a pathologist’s usual experience.
method: Used region-of-interest (ROI) images from whole-slide pathology slides as queries.
Compared four foundation models: Atlas2, Atlas2-B, Atlas2-S, and UNI2h.
Evaluated leave-one-case-out retrieval on 137 salivary gland tumor cases across 12 ICD-O morphology categories.
evidence_signal: Atlas2 achieved the strongest retrieval performance, with Top-1/3/5 accuracy of 62.5%/76.7%/81.3% and the best separation of correct vs incorrect matches in modified Chamfer similarity (AUC 0.754).
watch_item: Performance was tested on a relatively small, imbalanced single-dataset cohort, so broader validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Pathology foundation models for training-free case retrieval in salivary gland tumors
